content:
maya (oncall): :rotating_light: Paging: elevated p95 latency for hosted inference in us-west-2. Customers seeing slow responses ~>3000ms for short-chat flows. Root detection at 12:07 UTC.

sam (sre): I'm on it. grabbing current auto-scaling and recent deploys.

maya (oncall): signs: sudden p95 jump coincident with increased small-sequence traffic from a single IP range, plus QPS spike on route /v1/chat/stream.

devops-bot: Incident created: INC-1745600000. Severity: SEV2. Playbook: inference_latency.

andre (eng-runtime): quick check: no rolling deploys in the last 40m. kernel-metrics show rise in kernel scheduler stall on a subset of GPUs, NV-link errors intermittent on gw2-nodepool-4.

sam (sre): confirming. I see an enqueue backlog on async-batcher, per-worker queue depth up 4x. KV cache hitrate unchanged.

maya (oncall): impact: approximately 12% of production requests for hosted tier in us-west-2 with median payload len < 300 tokens; approximate customer impact list attached (internal): customer-A, customer-C, small-beta-2.

tess (support): I have two active customer chats asking about timeouts, escalating to us. Need a short status we can paste.

lucas (product): we should prepare both internal comms and a status page note. Keep wording minimal and avoid overpromising ETA.

sam (sre): mitigation plan step 1: fail traffic from problematic IP range to alternate region (us-east-1) via routing rule (temporary) to buy time. step 2: recycle gw2-nodepool-4 instances one-at-a-time. step 3: scale up reserved inference nodes for hosted tier by +15% for 30m.

andre (eng-runtime): agree. also toggle conservative batching (reduce max batch window from 30ms -> 5ms) to lower tail latency immediately. patch config on live with feature-flag.

maya (oncall): executing step 1 now: routing change in progress.

devops-bot: Routing change applied to route policy 'us-west-2-evade' at 12:15 UTC.

sam (sre): starting nodepool recycle, doing rolling restarts with drain. I'll monitor KV cache and batcher depth.

maya (oncall): tess, customer-friendly status draft below — please review: 

statuspage-bot (draft): "We are investigating elevated latency for inference in our US West region impacting a subset of customers. We are routing traffic to alternate capacity and performing targeted restarts. Some requests may experience delays or timeouts. We will post updates as we learn more."

tess (support): LGTM. add approximate ETA: initial mitigation in 10-15m.

lucas (product): suggested addition: "No data was lost. Customer requests are being routed; some may see temporary increased latency."

sam (sre): first recycle completed for gw2-nodepool-4-03. batcher depth down 30%. p95 improved from 3100ms -> 1800ms on that shard.

andre (eng-runtime): applied batching config change (FF: reduce_batch_window=true). Patch command: ```rbctl set-config inference.batch.max_wait_ms 5 --env hosted --region us-west-2```

devops-bot: Config change deployed (canary) at 12:21 UTC.

maya (oncall): routing + restarts + batch window lowered. monitoring for stabilization.

sam (sre): metrics: overall p95 across us-west-2 now 1100ms, still above target 350ms but trending down. error rate steady.

tess (support): sending high-level customer note to affected customers now (using template).

maya (oncall): prepare internal post-incident comms template for on-call handoff and blameless notes. draft below: 

postmortem-bot (draft-template): "Short summary: On <date> we observed elevated inference latency in us-west-2 affecting ~12% of requests. Timeline: detection -> mitigations (routing, restarts, batching change) -> partial recovery. Impact: increased request latency and some timeouts for short-chat workloads. Root cause hypothesis: one nodepool exhibited intermittent NV-link errors causing batcher enqueue/backpressure. Next steps: deeper hardware diagnostics, replace impacted instances, add IP-range throttling rule, and improve autoscale responsiveness + playbook additions."

lucas (product): good. include customer outreach note and who owns follow ups (SRE, Eng-runtime, Support).

andre (eng-runtime): note: we should add runtime metric to trigger earlier (batcher-backlog > 50ms queue) and alert before p95 crosses threshold. filing follow-up ticket.

maya (oncall): handoff to night oncall in 30m. summarizing handoff bullets: mitigation steps taken, current state (p95 900-1100ms, routing mostly live to alternate region for the problematic IP range), next actions (instance replacement tomorrow, autoscale tuning, postmortem action items).

sam (sre): leaving a runbook checkpoint: "if p95 < 600ms and error rate stable -> close incident after 1h of stable signals. if p95 > 1500ms -> re-escalate and consider temporary flow-control (rate-limit non-paying traces)."

maya (oncall): handoff ping to @night-oncall: please take over monitoring and customer comms, full notes in thread.

statuspage-bot: Public status updated at 12:35 UTC: "Degraded performance in US West. We have applied mitigations and continue to monitor. Some requests may still be slower than usual."

tess (support): notified affected customers: customer-A and customer-C acknowledged. one customer asked for timeline; I provided ETA ~2 hours for full recovery and escalation path.

sam (sre): current ETA: partial recovery now, full recovery contingent on instance replacement and autoscale tuning; expect 2-6 hours. keeping conservative.

andre (eng-runtime): created follow-ups: TASK-17456 (replace gw2-nodepool-4 hardware), TASK-17457 (add pre-p95 batching alert), TASK-17458 (postmortem).

maya (oncall): closing loop here for primary mitigation phase. leaving thread open for additional updates and handing to night shift. thanks all. :heart: 

lucas (product): thanks team — good coordination. we'll draft a short customer advisory tomorrow with details and root cause once confirmed."
